title: The Only Way to Save Global Order?
gist: An FP Live event page previewing Charles A. Kupchan's forthcoming book Bringing Order to Anarchy, which argues a historic diffusion of power is producing a bottom-up world order led by regional groupings, but that top-down governance remains essential—proposing a 19th-century Concert of Europe-style high-level brain trust to resolve great-power disputes above a paralyzed United Nations.

insights.claim: Charles Kupchan argues a historic diffusion of power is underway in which regional groupings grow in importance, setting the stage for a world order led from the bottom up rather than by a single hegemon.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: A bottom-up, regionalized order implies fragmenting global governance and rising importance of regional blocs—context for pricing multipolar geopolitical risk.
insights.quote: Regional groupings are growing in importance, setting the stage for a world order that will be led from the bottom-up.
insights.locator: In an upcoming essay for Foreign Policy

insights.claim: Kupchan proposes creating a high-level brain trust resembling the 19th-century Concert of Europe to resolve disputes between world powers and sit above a currently paralyzed United Nations.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: A great-power concert above the UN would be a major governance redesign; its feasibility shapes expectations for how future international disputes get managed.
insights.quote: a high-level brain trust resembling the 19th century Concert of Europe, which would step in to resolve disputes between world powers and sit above a currently paralyzed United Nations
insights.locator: Kupchan proposes the creation of a high-level brain trust

insights.claim: Kupchan holds that even as order becomes bottom-up, a measure of top-down governance will still remain essential.
insights.speaker: Dana Sherne
insights.so_what: The claim that pure multipolar diffusion is insufficient frames the debate over whether new supranational coordination mechanisms will emerge.
insights.quote: But a measure of top-down governance will still remain essential.
insights.locator: Regional groupings are growing in importance
